pr.title: Don't reset cast kind without also updating the operand in `simplify_cast` in GVN
pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: Nightly regressed igvm crate and now emits SIGILL at opt-level higher than 1
issues.body:
### Code I tried this code: https://github.com/durin42/igvm/commit/18802006ac0e946d412ba8b34385297eb2de4f03 `cargo +nightly test --release` I expected to see this happen: Tests all pass. Instead, this happened: Tests die with a SIGILL. ### Version it worked on This works on stable, and also up until b6b8361 (merge of #133324) ### Version with regression b6b8361 breaks, aka the merge of #133324. All nightlies since then show the same behavior. ### Backtrace I don't get one, I assume because it's a crash. ### bisect-rustc output: searched nightlies: from nightly-2025-01-07 to nightly-2025-01-13 regressed nightly: nightly-2025-01-10 searched commit range: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/compare/a580b5c379b4fca50dfe5afc0fc0ce00921e4e00...824759493246ee383beb9cd5ceffa0e15deb9fa4 regressed commit: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/b6b8361bce8561fb8786ad33ca1abfdf4bc487b6
bisected with cargo-bisect-rustc v0.6.8 Host triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu Reproduce with: ```bash cargo bisect-rustc --start 2025-01-07 --end 2025-01-13 -- test --release ```
It's plausible to me that one of the crates in here is guilty of some unsafe crimes, but I'm not sure how to prove who's at fault at this point. @rustbot modify labels: +regression-from-stable-to-nightly -regression-untriaged

issues.title: invalid opcode regression in `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` release builds while compiling code using `generic-array`

processing.reason: The source-grounded rewrite is a GVN bug that changes the final cast kind to `Transmute` while the operand remains the original wide `*const [()]`/`*mut [T]` local, producing a MIR transmute between a wide pointer and a thin pointer. That historical wrong transformation is itself ill-typed/undefined (size-mismatched transmute), not a defined Rust operation. A faithful runtime encoding with `transmute_copy::<*const [()], *mut ()>` was tested and, as expected on this little-endian pointer representation, produced exactly the same data address as the valid `PtrToPtr` cast (4096 for both original and transformed under Miri/O0/O3). Producing differing defined values would require inventing a semantics for the invalid transmute (e.g. reinterpreting the wide pointer's length/metadata word as the thin pointer), which is not the historical transformation and would be an arbitrary model of UB. The actual regression evidence is the malformed MIR dump (and the resulting undefined codegen/SIGILL), not a defined runtime value, so no legitimate Miri-passing original/transformed pair with differing concrete results can be validated from this source.

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's `simplify_cast` received the assignment's cast kind and operand as `&mut CastKind`/`&mut Operand`, simplified the operand to a value node, then iterated: it could rewrite the cast kind (e.g. `*kind = PtrToPtr` when `from` and `to` are both unsafe pointers with matching metadata, or set `*kind = new_kind` when folding a `PtrToPtr` whose operand is itself a `Transmute`), and at the end, if anything was updated, tried `self.try_as_operand(value, location)` to replace the operand with the simplified value. Only if that succeeded did it write `*operand = op`. In the pre-fix code the kind had already been mutated in place regardless, and the final value node was inserted with `Value::Cast { kind: *kind, value, from, to }`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Changing the final cast's `CastKind` (to `Transmute`, or folding a PtrToPtr-of-Transmute into a single Transmute) without simultaneously replacing the cast operand, because `try_to_operand`/`try_as_operand` failed. GVN "only turns value nodes into locals or consts, not projections of locals", so when the simplified value was a place projection the operand stayed as the original wide pointer local, producing MIR like `_7 = copy _5 as *mut () (Transmute)` where `_5: *const [()]` is a wide pointer and `*mut ()` is a thin pointer. That is a transmute between types of different sizes, the confirmed regression. The correct behavior is to leave the cast kind unchanged (keep the originally valid `PtrToPtr`) and only commit the new kind when the operand is also replaced.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR after `Inline` on safe code that builds a raw slice-of-unit pointer from a thin pointer via `std::ptr::slice_from_raw_parts`/`from_raw_parts`, then casts the `*const [()]` back to a thin `*mut ()`/`*const ()`. Simplified casts include unsized->sized `PtrToPtr` whose operand is `AggregateKind::RawPtr`, and nested `Transmute` casts (e.g. `Unique<()> -> NonNull<()> -> *const ()`). The problematic case is when the simplified cast value is a projection of a local (not a local/const), so `try_as_operand` returns `None`.
analysis.summary: Confirmed GVN bug fix: `simplify_cast` mutated the caller's `CastKind` while iterating even when the operand rewrite failed, yielding a `Transmute` between a wide (`*const [()]`) and a thin (`*mut ()`) pointer. The fix keeps the kind in a local, commits `initial_kind` only together with a successfully updated `initial_operand`, and inserts the value node with the local kind.
analysis.trigger: GVN simplifies a cast chain involving an unsized->sized `PtrToPtr` (operand an `AggregateKind::RawPtr`) and/or a `PtrToPtr` whose operand is a `Transmute`; the resulting value is a projection of a local, so the operand replacement fails while a kind update was still applied.
preconditions: The cast is being visited by GVN's `simplify_cast` with an existing valid kind (e.g. `PtrToPtr`).
An optimization iteration decides to change the kind (metadata-compatible PtrToPtr rewrite, or Transmute folding).
The simplified value node cannot be turned into an operand by `try_as_operand` (e.g. it is a projection of a local rather than a local or const).
The original operand and destination have different sizes (wide unsized pointer vs thin pointer), so an unpaired Transmute is semantically invalid.
pitfalls: Do not conflate the actual bug with the harmless copy propagation `_8 = copy _5` / `_8` being replaced by `_5`; the retained fixed test still contains `_8 = copy _5` and `_7 = copy _5 as *mut () (PtrToPtr)`. The bug is the kind change, not copy propagation.
The fix does not prevent simplification; it only defers committing the kind until the operand is also replaced. A `Transmute` is still allowed when the operand genuinely becomes the inner value.
Do not claim execution/reproduction of the SIGILL; no compiler was built, and the evidence is the MIR dump.
The test is `// skip-filecheck` and uses `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`; it validates MIR output, not runtime behavior.
Borrowing restrictions and post-copy overwrites are separate conditions and are not the cause here.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a `tests/mir-opt` test with `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+Inline,+GVN --crate-type lib`, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, `// EMIT_MIR dont_reset_cast_kind_without_updating_operand.test.GVN.diff`, and `// skip-filecheck`. Construct input with `Box<()>`, `&raw const **vp_ctx`, `std::ptr::slice_from_raw_parts(slf, 1)`, then `fn foo(bytes: *const [()]) -> *mut () { bytes as *mut () }`. Assert in the MIR dump that the final cast is `_7 = copy _5 as *mut () (PtrToPtr)` (wide-to-thin) and NOT `... (Transmute)`. To isolate the transformation, compare two programs differing only in whether the simplified value is a local/const (operand update succeeds, Transmute may be valid) versus a place projection (operand update fails, kind must stay PtrToPtr).
evidence: we must *not* update the CastKind of the final cast *unless* we also update the operand of the cast, since the operand may no longer make sense with the updated CastKind.

because GVN only turns value nodes into locals or consts, not projections of locals. So we fail to update the operand, but we still update the CastKind to Transmute, which means we now are transmuting types of different sizes (a wide pointer and a thin pointer).
